questions.stem: Which of the following best defines economic planning?

options.text: The process of setting goals and determining the actions to achieve them.
A method of distributing resources randomly.
The practice of allowing market forces to dictate economic outcomes.
A strategy to eliminate all forms of government intervention.

questions.explanation: Economic planning involves setting specific goals for the economy and outlining the actions needed to achieve those goals. This process helps in resource allocation and prioritization of development objectives.

distractorRationale.b: This option misrepresents economic planning as it requires systematic allocation rather than random distribution.
distractorRationale.c: This option describes a laissez-faire approach, which is contrary to the concept of economic planning.
distractorRationale.d: This option suggests complete non-intervention, which is not aligned with the objectives of economic planning.

questions.stem: What is one major advantage of having a rolling plan in economic planning?

options.text: It allows for the adjustment of plans based on changing circumstances.

questions.explanation: A rolling plan is designed to be flexible and adaptable, allowing policymakers to revise and update their strategies as new data and circumstances arise. This adaptability is crucial for responding to economic changes effectively.

distractorRationale.b: The cost of implementation can vary; rolling plans do not inherently mean lower costs.
distractorRationale.c: While rolling plans can lead to improvements, they do not guarantee immediate results.
distractorRationale.d: Government oversight is still necessary in rolling plans to ensure accountability and effectiveness.
